verdicts.reason: Both drop the SOLSTICE can from the hero panel. What's left is an empty purple rectangle, plus a thumbnail-sized can stuck in the bottom-left corner, and the logo sits right-aligned off the text grid. A also puts the empty image above the headline, so the eye lands on nothing first. B leads with the headline and subcopy, which is a better reading order, but its CTA is jammed against the bottom of the image.

A loses the product entirely: the image box is empty and the can is shrunk to a speck in the bottom-left. Its logo is also off-axis. B keeps the can and the original two-column layout, but it is just the banner shrunk into a band in the middle, with about 220px of dead space above and below. Its subcopy and CTA text are small. B still wins because the hero product and brand survive.

A has a top-placed image box that shows nothing, and the can is reduced to a tiny orphan in the bottom-left. The product is effectively lost. B keeps the can image intact but breaks the grouping. The headline, the tiny subcopy and the CTA are spread down the left column with big unexplained gaps, and the logo floats far above everything else. B is less bad only because it keeps the product.

A keeps the product image, but the left-column text is scattered. Subcopy and CTA are cut off from the headline by large gaps, the subcopy is tiny, and the logo sits isolated at the top. B has clean type hierarchy and margins but shows an empty purple image box. Its can is shrunk to an unreadable corner icon, and the logo is right-aligned off the grid. Losing the hero product is the bigger fidelity failure.
